about: Sentences written from the text of dev pull requests, labelled by how their fixed code handles the failure, read from the diff (#85, ADR 0026, written-85/README.md). Built by written-85/combine.ts.

sentences.label: failure_handling
sentences.text: When decoding a value fails on a decode path, the profiler must surface the error instead of silently turning it into missing data or a default value that it treats as a statistic.

sentences.label: failure_propagation
sentences.text: cce doctor must report a present but invalid workspace.yml as a definite-corruption failure and exit non-zero instead of silently degrading to single-directory mode, and cce sync pull must refuse to overwrite the local index at a different sha without --force when .cce/synced.json is present but corrupt.

sentences.label: failure_propagation
sentences.text: When building a proposal, answering a sync request, or building or refreshing the validator set, failures in tx parsing, DB queries, protobuf/value encoding, and certificate encoding must be propagated as errors with context instead of being silently dropped, and invalid staking data must fail validator-set building rather than skip the validator.

sentences.label: failure_propagation
sentences.text: When serializing the result of an MCP tool call fails, the server must return an error response to the client instead of empty content.

sentences.label: failure_handling
sentences.text: When an OCPP or Modbus module view stops or (re)starts its backend on a settings change, version switch, or stop/restart/reload command, a failure of that stop or start shall be reported in the module message log at Error level rather than silently discarded.

sentences.label: failure_handling
sentences.text: Errors must not be silently swallowed: a failure while collecting build inputs must be propagated instead of dropping the entry from the build cache key, `pybun python which` must surface the underlying discovery error instead of reporting only that no Python was found, and drift analysis must report unreadable .py files to the user instead of silently skipping them.

sentences.label: failure_handling
sentences.text: When killing, cancelling or stopping a connection or session fails, the failure must be logged and shown to the user, and the still-live connection must stay listed instead of the action looking like it succeeded.

sentences.label: failure_handling
sentences.text: Every remaining production .catch(() => {}) on a mutating or teardown path must route its failure to the LogViewer via frontendError, or be wrapped in the fireAndForget(promise, reason) helper with a stated reason, instead of silently swallowing it.

sentences.label: failure_handling
sentences.text: coordinate() must not panic when SQLite returns SQLITE_BUSY or SQLITE_LOCKED under heavy concurrency, but must let the error reach the existing outer backoff loop and retry.

sentences.label: failure_propagation
sentences.text: When loading the root node or rewriting tree heights fails during Restorer::finalize, the error must be reported to the caller instead of being silently discarded.

sentences.label: failure_propagation
sentences.text: Restorer::process_chunk must propagate an error from set_base_root_key instead of silently discarding it and continuing to restore on corrupt state.

sentences.label: failure_handling
sentences.text: When persisting a rack health report fails, the failure must be logged and counted instead of being silently discarded.

sentences.label: failure_propagation
sentences.text: Credential and profile writes must report failures instead of swallowing them: the durable atomic write must fail if flushing, syncing, or setting 0600 permissions fails, the alias command must abort rather than overwrite a shell profile it could not read, and isolate setup must warn when linking host files or writing isolate.json fails.

sentences.label: failure_propagation
sentences.text: The gRPC state reader must propagate useful errors to the user, including for getting the latest checkpoint sequence number, instead of panicking or silently returning None.

sentences.label: failure_propagation
sentences.text: When a fetch fails, the error must be reported instead of being swallowed.

sentences.label: failure_handling
sentences.text: agent_message must not report delivered for a target_session_id whose session has already finished, returning target_session_finished instead, and must not report target_agent_not_found for an agent that is installed through the alias registry.

sentences.label: failure_propagation
sentences.text: When auto-title generation for a session fails, the sessions.generate_title RPC and the channel /title command must report the failure instead of returning `label: null`.

sentences.label: failure_propagation
sentences.text: When downloading an external snapshot or mutation blob during app state sync fails, the failure must propagate so that the collection version is not advanced past data the client failed to fetch.

sentences.label: failure_propagation
sentences.text: Recurring enqueue, for both cron execution and manual run-now, must propagate an error from resolving a job's concurrency constraint, naming the recurring task key, instead of swallowing it and inserting an unrestricted ready job.

sentences.label: failure_propagation
sentences.text: Transliteration and typing APIs must surface errors consistently across platforms and bindings as explicit errors instead of silently ignoring them or returning null.

sentences.label: failure_handling
sentences.text: `omamori doctor` must report `[Staging] empty` or a file count only for a staging directory it read in full, and otherwise must say it cannot read it instead of reporting it empty.

sentences.label: failure_handling
sentences.text: When hook-check --json-error blocks a command, it must record the block in the audit chain exactly as in text mode while keeping stderr a single JSON object.

sentences.label: failure_propagation
sentences.text: append() must chain onto the log's last chain entry, and content after it that is not a chain entry must never make append() start a second chain or lift its refusal after an unrecognized chain_version.
